main_text.p: 5. An sepulturæ extra urbem sint habendæ, & an omnes homines sint sepeliendi. A.
main_text.head: Justa Lex Regit Homines,

p.i: Disputabuntur in Collegio philosophico hora & loco solitis.

main_text.head: AD PHILOSOPHIAE CANDI-datum Johannem Langium familiarem suum.

p.i: FRIGIDUS, aëria, nix & velut imber ab axe Descendunt primo vere ineunte modo. Ultra[illegible, ~2 letters] remeant illuc, sine frugibus unquam Arida: sed reddunt, pinguia, rura, prius. Sic etiam ingenuâ tempus qui fallit in arte, Non labor, absq; huius fruge peractus abit. Sed multos templis fructus parit, ante, scholisq; Et patriæ fidâ dexteritate præest. Artes ingenuæ siquidem sunt splendida dona, Aequore quæ nullo aut igne famève ruunt. Tela ergo è nitidâ, Langi, depromè pharetrâ, Inq[?]; hostes, forti pectore mitte tuos. Sic solus reliquis clarus, præ, victor abibis Contentus, viridi fronde tegente caput. Aureolam, æternâ, capies dum luce, coronam, Omnia, quæ viridi, secula fronde viget.

page.notes: The first word of the poem is a large initial F, read as FRIGIDUS (printed FRIGIDVS). "Ultra" is followed by a blurred word, marked illegible. "Inq;" in line 12 is uncertain. A small ornament (§§ with flourishes) between the title and the dedication is not text and is left out. A blue library stamp near the foot and show-through are left out. No page number or running head is printed.
